topics.description: Understand NoSQL concepts and MongoDB fundamentals: documents, collections, BSON, and when to choose document databases.
topics.goal: Explain MongoDB's document model and use it for simple data storage needs.

topics.title: Data Modeling in MongoDB
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Schema design patterns: embedding vs referencing
topics.description: Learn embedding vs referencing, schema design patterns, modelling one-to-many relationships, and trade-offs for read/write patterns.
topics.goal: Design an efficient document model for a sample application.

topics.title: CRUD and Aggregation Framework
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Powerful queries
topics.description: Perform CRUD operations, and use the aggregation framework for transforms, grouping, and analytics within the database.
topics.goal: Write aggregation pipelines to reshape and summarise data.

topics.title: Indexing and Query Performance
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Optimize queries
topics.description: Understand indexes, index types, explain plans, and strategies to improve read performance while balancing write costs.
topics.goal: Add appropriate indexes and interpret explain output to optimise queries.

topics.title: Replication and High Availability
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Replication sets
topics.description: Configure replica sets for redundancy, understand election behavior, read preferences, and how to operate a highly available cluster.
topics.goal: Design a replica set for fault tolerance and failover.

topics.title: Sharding and Scalability
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Partitioning data
topics.description: Learn sharding fundamentals, choosing shard keys, balancing, and considerations for large-scale MongoDB deployments.
topics.goal: Plan a sharded deployment for heavy-write workloads.

topics.title: Backups, Security and Operations
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Production readiness: backups, security, and monitoring
topics.description: Perform backups and restores, secure MongoDB (authentication, authorization, encryption), and monitor health and resource usage.
topics.goal: Implement backup and security best-practices for a MongoDB deployment.

topics.title: Redux Pattern & NgRX Overview
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Why state management matters, Redux mental model, NgRX ecosystem
topics.description: Covers the problem that global state management solves, the Flux/Redux mental model (single source of truth, state is read-only, changes through pure functions), how NgRX implements Redux for Angular, and a tour of the NgRX package ecosystem: @ngrx/store, @ngrx/effects, @ngrx/entity, @ngrx/router-store, @ngrx/component-store, and @ngrx/signals.
topics.goal: Explain why unidirectional data flow matters, describe the Redux cycle (action → reducer → store → selector → view), and identify which NgRX package solves which problem.

topics.title: NgRX Store & DevTools
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: provideStore, feature state, and Redux DevTools debugging
topics.description: Covers bootstrapping the NgRX store with provideStore() and provideState() in a standalone Angular application, defining feature state slices, registering the StoreDevtools module for time-travel debugging, inspecting dispatched actions and state snapshots in the Redux DevTools browser extension, and understanding the global state tree.
topics.goal: Bootstrap a working NgRX store in an Angular application, register feature states, and use Redux DevTools to inspect and replay state changes.

topics.title: Actions
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: createAction, createActionGroup, and dispatching typed actions
topics.description: Covers creating typed actions with createAction() and props<T>(), grouping related actions with createActionGroup() to reduce boilerplate, NgRX action naming conventions (describing events rather than commands), dispatching actions from components and services via Store.dispatch(), and understanding actions as the single communication channel into the store.
topics.goal: Define strongly-typed actions using createAction and createActionGroup, follow naming conventions, and dispatch actions from Angular components and services.

topics.title: Reducers & State
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: createReducer, on(), and enforcing immutable state updates
topics.description: Covers defining initial state with TypeScript interfaces, writing pure reducer functions with createReducer() and on(), enforcing immutability (spread operator and structured clone patterns), understanding how reducers are composed into the global state tree, and registering feature reducers with provideState().
topics.goal: Write pure, immutable reducers with createReducer that correctly handle multiple actions and compose into the global NgRX state tree.

topics.title: Selectors
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: createSelector, memoization, and Signal-based selection
topics.description: Covers createFeatureSelector() to access feature state slices, composing selectors with createSelector(), memoization and why it prevents unnecessary re-renders, projector functions for derived data, selecting state in components with store.select() and the modern store.selectSignal() for Angular Signals integration, and selector testing strategies.
topics.goal: Build a selector hierarchy using createSelector and createFeatureSelector, understand memoization, and connect selectors to Angular components using both observables and selectSignal().

topics.title: NgRX Effects
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: createEffect, Actions$ stream, and flattening operators
topics.description: Covers side-effect management with createEffect(), the Actions$ stream and ofType() operator, choosing the right flattening operator (switchMap for cancellable, concatMap for sequential, exhaustMap for ignoring concurrent, mergeMap for parallel), handling errors with catchError and returning failure actions, dispatch: false for non-dispatching effects, and testing effects with provideMockActions.
topics.goal: Handle HTTP calls and other async side effects with NgRX Effects, choose the correct RxJS flattening operator for the use case, and handle errors gracefully without crashing the effect stream.

topics.title: NgRX Entity
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: EntityAdapter, CRUD methods, and normalised collection state
topics.description: Covers the motivation for @ngrx/entity (normalised collection state), creating an EntityAdapter with createEntityAdapter(), the EntityState shape (ids array + entities dictionary), built-in CRUD adapter methods (addOne, addMany, setAll, updateOne, upsertOne, removeOne, removeMany), and the pre-built selector factory (selectAll, selectEntities, selectIds, selectTotal). Includes a brief introduction to @ngrx/data for high-level CRUD abstraction.
topics.goal: Manage normalised entity collections in NgRX using EntityAdapter, reduce reducer boilerplate for CRUD operations, and query entities efficiently with the generated selectors.

topics.title: NgRX Router Store
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Router state, router selectors, and navigation from effects
topics.description: Covers connecting Angular Router state to the NgRX store with provideRouterStore() and routerReducer, using the built-in router selectors (selectRouteParam, selectQueryParam, selectUrl, selectRouteData), triggering navigation from NgRX effects using Angular Router, serialising minimal router state for performance, and reading route information from the store rather than directly injecting ActivatedRoute.
topics.goal: Integrate Angular Router state into the NgRX store, query URL parameters and route data via selectors, and trigger programmatic navigation from effects.

topics.title: Component Store
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Local state, updaters, and the vm$ ViewModel pattern
topics.description: Covers @ngrx/component-store as a solution for local component-level state (avoiding global store pollution), defining state with ComponentStore<T>, mutating state with updater() and patchState(), reading state reactively with select() and the vm$ ViewModel pattern, handling async operations with the built-in effect(), and deciding when to use ComponentStore versus the global store versus plain Angular Signals.
topics.goal: Manage component-scoped state with ComponentStore, expose a clean ViewModel observable to templates, and choose appropriately between local and global state solutions.

topics.title: NgRX Signals Store
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: SignalStore, withState, withComputed, and rxMethod
topics.description: Covers @ngrx/signals as the modern signal-native state primitive, creating a SignalStore with signalStore(), composing store features with withState(), withComputed(), withMethods(), withEntities(), and withHooks(), bridging RxJS with signals using rxMethod(), updating state atomically with patchState(), building custom store features for reuse, and understanding how NgRX Signals relates to and differs from the classic @ngrx/store.
topics.goal: Build reactive, signal-based state stores with @ngrx/signals, compose reusable store features, and integrate RxJS-based async logic via rxMethod().

topics.title: Angular Modules
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: NgModule system
topics.description: Understand how NgModule organises an Angular app into cohesive blocks — covering declarations, imports, exports, providers, and the difference between feature and shared modules.
topics.goal: Describe the role of NgModule, set up feature modules, create shared modules, and understand how Angular resolves components and services at the module level.

topics.title: Custom Pipes
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Build your own pipe
topics.description: Go beyond Angular's built-in pipes by creating reusable, parameterised transformation pipes using the @Pipe decorator and PipeTransform interface.
topics.goal: Create pure and impure custom pipes, pass parameters via the pipe syntax, declare them in modules, and understand performance implications.

topics.title: Lazy Loading
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: On-demand modules
topics.description: Split your app into feature modules that load only when needed, dramatically reducing initial bundle size and improving startup performance.
topics.goal: Configure lazy-loaded routes with loadChildren, apply PreloadAllModules and custom preloading strategies, and verify bundle splits in the build output.

topics.title: Advanced Change Detection
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: OnPush & zones
topics.description: Master Angular's change detection engine: the difference between Default and OnPush strategies, Zone.js internals, manual triggering, and detach/reattach patterns.
topics.goal: Apply ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush correctly, use ChangeDetectorRef to trigger or skip checks, and run tasks outside NgZone for performance gains.

topics.title: Component State Patterns
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: State strategies
topics.description: Explore patterns for managing local and shared component state: smart vs presentational components, BehaviorSubject services, and when to reach for a state library.
topics.goal: Choose the right state strategy for a given feature, implement a reactive shared-state service with BehaviorSubject, and avoid common anti-patterns like nested subscriptions.

topics.title: NgRx
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Redux state for Angular: Store, Actions, Reducers, Selectors, Effects
topics.description: Manage application state predictably with NgRx: Store, Actions, Reducers, Selectors, and Effects for complex, testable data flows.
topics.goal: Implement a feature slice with NgRx, dispatch typed actions, derive state with memoized selectors, and handle API side effects with Effects.

topics.title: Angular Signals
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Reactive primitives
topics.description: Explore Angular's built-in signal primitives (Angular 17+): signal(), computed(), and effect(), enabling fine-grained reactivity without Zone.js overhead.
topics.goal: Replace BehaviorSubjects with signals where appropriate, derive computed values, react to changes with effects, and understand the signal-based change detection model.

topics.title: Advanced RxJS
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: RxJS deep dive
topics.description: Move beyond basic map and catchError: multicasting, higher-order observables, backpressure, custom operators, and patterns for complex async workflows in Angular.
topics.goal: Use switchMap, concatMap, mergeMap, and exhaustMap correctly, implement multicasting with shareReplay, write custom RxJS operators, and avoid common memory-leak pitfalls.

topics.title: Performance Optimization
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Speed & efficiency
topics.description: Identify and fix Angular performance bottlenecks: bundle analysis, tree-shaking, defer blocks, virtual scrolling, trackBy, and image optimisation.
topics.goal: Profile an Angular app with Chrome DevTools, reduce bundle size with source-map-explorer, apply @defer for heavy components, and implement virtual scrolling for large lists.

topics.title: Core Web Vitals
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: LCP · CLS · INP
topics.description: Understand and optimise the three Google Core Web Vitals — Largest Contentful Paint, Cumulative Layout Shift, and Interaction to Next Paint — in the context of Angular SPAs.
topics.goal: Measure LCP, CLS, and INP using Lighthouse and web-vitals.js, identify Angular-specific causes of each metric degrading, and apply targeted fixes.

topics.title: Server-Side Rendering
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Angular Universal / @angular/ssr for SEO and faster First Contentful Paint
topics.description: Render Angular applications on the server with Angular Universal (now built into Angular 17+ via @angular/ssr) for improved SEO, First Contentful Paint, and Time to Interactive.
topics.goal: Add SSR to an existing Angular project, handle browser-only APIs safely, implement hydration, and deploy a Node.js SSR server.

topics.title: Angular Security
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: XSS · CSRF · auth
topics.description: Understand Angular's built-in XSS protections, use DomSanitizer correctly, implement CSRF mitigation, attach JWT tokens via HTTP interceptors, and follow OWASP guidelines.
topics.goal: Identify common Angular security pitfalls, write a JWT auth interceptor, sanitize dynamic HTML safely, and configure Content Security Policy headers.

topics.title: Testing
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Unit & integration
topics.description: Write reliable unit and integration tests for Angular components, services, and pipes using Jasmine, Karma, and Angular TestBed, with mocked HTTP via HttpClientTestingModule.
topics.goal: Test a component with TestBed, mock services with spies, verify template output, test reactive forms, and simulate HTTP requests without hitting real APIs.

topics.title: Dynamic Components
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Runtime component creation with ViewContainerRef, ComponentRef, @defer
topics.description: Create and insert Angular components programmatically at runtime using ViewContainerRef, ComponentRef, and the new @defer and @if control flow blocks.
topics.goal: Dynamically render a component into a container, pass inputs at runtime, destroy components cleanly, and build a simple modal or tooltip system.

topics.title: Standalone Components
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Modern bootstrapping without NgModules: bootstrapApplication, standalone: true
topics.description: Learn Angular's modern module-free API: bootstrapApplication(), standalone: true, provideRouter(), importProvidersFrom(), and the standalone component mental model.
topics.goal: Migrate a module-based feature to standalone, bootstrap an app without AppModule, and understand how DI works without NgModule boundaries.

topics.title: Error Handling
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Errors & interceptors: ErrorHandler, HTTP interceptors, retry strategies
topics.description: Build resilient Angular apps: global ErrorHandler, HTTP error interceptors, retry strategies with RxJS, user-facing error states, and structured error boundaries.
topics.goal: Implement a global ErrorHandler, write an HTTP interceptor that retries on 5xx errors, and present meaningful feedback to users on failures.

topics.title: Content Projection
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: ng-content & slots
topics.description: Compose reusable component APIs using ng-content, multi-slot projection with select, ContentChild, ContentChildren, and ng-template with TemplateRef.
topics.goal: Build a card component with named slots, project conditional content, and query projected children with ContentChild.

topics.title: Custom Directives
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Attribute & structural directives with ElementRef, Renderer2, TemplateRef
topics.description: Extend HTML with custom behaviour: build attribute directives with ElementRef, Renderer2, @HostListener, @HostBinding, and write simple structural directives with TemplateRef and ViewContainerRef.
topics.goal: Create an attribute directive that changes element style on hover, and a structural directive that conditionally renders content with context data.

topics.title: Advanced Forms
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: CVA & FormArray
topics.description: Go beyond basic reactive forms: ControlValueAccessor for custom form controls, FormArray for dynamic fields, cross-field validators, nested FormGroups, and typed reactive forms.
topics.goal: Implement a custom form control with ControlValueAccessor, build a dynamic field list with FormArray, and add a cross-field validator to a FormGroup.

topics.title: Advanced Routing
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Resolvers & outlets
topics.description: Master Angular router's advanced capabilities: route resolvers for pre-fetching data, named/secondary router outlets, route parameters and query params strategies, and functional guards.
topics.goal: Write a route resolver that fetches data before navigation, implement named outlets for a side-panel layout, and convert class-based guards to functional guards.

topics.title: Angular Animations
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Motion & transitions with triggers, states, keyframes, and stagger
topics.description: Add motion to Angular apps with @angular/animations: triggers, states, transitions, keyframes, animateChild, and query/stagger for list animations.
topics.goal: Animate a route transition, build an expanding panel with state-based animation, and stagger a list of items on entry.

topics.title: Angular CDK
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Component Dev Kit
topics.description: Use Angular CDK to build robust UI primitives: Overlay for popups/tooltips, Portal for dynamic content, DragDrop for sortable lists, FocusTrap for accessibility, and virtual scrolling.
topics.goal: Build a custom tooltip using CDK Overlay, implement drag-and-drop reordering with CdkDragDrop, and trap focus inside a modal with FocusTrap.

topics.title: PWA & Service Workers
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Offline & push
topics.description: Convert an Angular app into a Progressive Web App using @angular/service-worker: caching strategies, offline support, push notifications, app update flows, and Web App Manifest.
topics.goal: Add service worker support to an Angular app, configure asset and data caching strategies in ngsw-config.json, and prompt users to reload when a new version deploys.

topics.title: i18n
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Internationalisation with $localize, extract-i18n, and locale-aware pipes
topics.description: Internationalise Angular apps using built-in i18n with $localize, the Angular CLI extract-i18n workflow, locale-aware pipes (date, currency, number), and ngx-translate for runtime language switching.
topics.goal: Mark strings for translation, extract message files with ng extract-i18n, build locale-specific bundles, and implement runtime language switching with ngx-translate.

topics.title: Command Line Basics
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Navigating files & directories with cd, ls, pwd, cat, man
topics.description: Move around the filesystem, list and inspect files, and use core commands like cd, ls, pwd, cat, and man.
topics.goal: Navigate a Linux filesystem confidently from the terminal.

topics.title: File Permissions & Ownership
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: chmod, chown, ownership, and the Linux permission model
topics.description: Understand the Linux permission model (owner/group/other, read/write/execute) and how to change permissions and ownership with chmod and chown.
topics.goal: Read and modify file permissions to secure or share files correctly.

topics.title: Shell Scripting Basics
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Variables, loops, and automating tasks with bash scripts
topics.description: Write simple bash scripts using variables, conditionals, and loops to automate repetitive command-line tasks.
topics.goal: Write and run a basic shell script that automates a multi-step task.

topics.title: Metrics & Dashboards
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Prometheus, Grafana metrics collection and visualization
topics.description: Understand what metrics are, how they're collected (e.g. Prometheus) and visualized on dashboards (e.g. Grafana).
topics.goal: Explain the difference between a metric, a dashboard panel, and an alert.

topics.title: Logging Fundamentals
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Structured logs, log levels, and centralized aggregation
topics.description: Understand structured logging, log levels (debug/info/warn/error), and centralized log aggregation.
topics.goal: Explain why structured logs are easier to search and alert on than plain text logs.

topics.title: Alerting Basics
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Thresholds, on-call, and avoiding alert fatigue
topics.description: Understand how alerting thresholds are set, what makes a good alert, and how alert fatigue happens.
topics.goal: Distinguish a well-designed alert from a noisy one and explain why it matters for on-call.

topics.title: REST Fundamentals & Resource Design
topics.label: Foundation
topics.description: What REST actually means, the constraints that define it, and how to model resources and URLs the RESTful way.
topics.goal: Learner can design a clean, resource-oriented URL structure for a new API.

topics.title: HTTP Methods & Status Codes
topics.label: Foundation
topics.description: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, and the status codes that tell a client exactly what happened.
topics.goal: Learner can pick the correct method and status code for any API operation, unprompted.

topics.title: Request & Response Design
topics.label: Foundation
topics.description: Headers, content negotiation, and structuring JSON bodies so every endpoint feels like it belongs to the same API.
topics.goal: Learner can design a consistent request/response contract for a new endpoint.

topics.title: Pagination, Filtering & Sorting
topics.label: Foundation
topics.description: Query-parameter patterns for handling large collections without overloading the client or the server.
topics.goal: Learner can design a list endpoint that stays fast at 10 rows and at 10 million.

topics.title: Authentication & Authorization Basics
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.description: The difference between who are you and what can you do, and comparing API keys, sessions, and JWTs.
topics.goal: Learner can choose the right authentication strategy for a given API use case.

topics.title: OAuth 2.0 & Social Login
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.description: The OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow end to end, and exactly how Sign in with Google and Sign in with LinkedIn work under the hood.
topics.goal: Learner can implement and reason about a working Google or LinkedIn sign-in flow, including what goes wrong when a step is skipped.

topics.title: API Versioning & Evolution
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.description: URL versioning, header versioning, and how to deprecate an endpoint without breaking the clients depending on it.
topics.goal: Learner can plan a breaking change that doesn't break anyone currently using the API.

topics.title: Error Handling & Validation
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.description: Consistent error response shapes, and validating input before it ever reaches business logic.
topics.goal: Learner can design error responses a client can handle programmatically, not just read.

topics.title: API Security Hardening
topics.label: Advanced
topics.description: CORS, HTTPS/TLS, and the OWASP API Security Top 10 — the defenses that stop an API from becoming the easiest way into a system.
topics.goal: Learner can audit an endpoint against common API attack patterns and close the obvious gaps.

topics.title: Caching Strategies for APIs
topics.label: Advanced
topics.description: ETags, Cache-Control, and conditional requests — how APIs avoid doing the same expensive work twice for the same answer.
topics.goal: Learner can add correct caching headers to a read-heavy endpoint without ever serving stale data.

topics.title: Idempotency, Retries & Resilience
topics.label: Advanced
topics.description: Idempotency keys, safe retries, timeouts, and circuit breakers — the patterns that keep a flaky network from double-charging a customer.
topics.goal: Learner can design a POST endpoint that's safe to retry.

topics.title: Rate Limiting & Throttling
topics.label: Advanced
topics.description: Why APIs need limits, the common algorithms (token bucket, sliding window), and how limits get communicated back to a client.
topics.goal: Learner can design and explain a rate-limiting strategy for a public API.

topics.title: Testing & Documenting APIs
topics.label: Advanced
topics.description: Testing endpoints with Postman and automated suites, and documenting them so someone else can actually use them.
topics.goal: Learner can write and maintain an OpenAPI spec that matches the real API.

topics.title: Cloud Computing & AWS Fundamentals
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Cloud basics & AWS
topics.description: Cloud computing vs. on-premises, the six benefits of cloud computing (trade capex for opex, elasticity, stop guessing capacity, and more), the AWS Free Tier, the Management Console, and the CLI.
topics.goal: Explain the core benefits of cloud computing and launch a basic resource from the AWS Management Console.

topics.title: AWS Global Infrastructure
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Regions & AZs
topics.description: Regions, Availability Zones, and Edge Locations — how AWS's physical infrastructure drives availability, latency, and disaster recovery decisions.
topics.goal: Choose an appropriate Region and multi-AZ design for a latency-sensitive, highly available application.

topics.title: Compute on AWS
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: EC2, scaling & ELB
topics.description: EC2 instance types and pricing models (On-Demand, Reserved, Spot, Savings Plans), Auto Scaling, and Elastic Load Balancing for distributing traffic across healthy instances.
topics.goal: Pick the right EC2 pricing model and configure Auto Scaling with a load balancer for a variable-traffic workload.

topics.title: Storage on AWS
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: S3, EBS & EFS
topics.description: Instance store vs. EBS vs. S3 vs. EFS — durability, performance, and cost trade-offs across AWS's core storage services.
topics.goal: Match a workload's durability and access-pattern requirements to the correct AWS storage service.

topics.title: Databases on AWS
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: RDS, DynamoDB & more: managed relational, NoSQL, and data warehousing
topics.description: Managed relational databases with RDS, NoSQL with DynamoDB, when to choose DynamoDB over RDS, Redshift for data warehousing, and DMS for migrating existing databases.
topics.goal: Choose between RDS and DynamoDB for a given data model and justify the decision.

topics.title: Networking & Provisioning
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: VPC, CloudFormation
topics.description: VPCs, subnets, and connectivity options, plus infrastructure-as-code and managed deployment with CloudFormation and Elastic Beanstalk.
topics.goal: Design a VPC with public and private subnets and provision it with a CloudFormation template.

topics.title: Serverless & Containers
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Lambda, ECS, EKS
topics.description: Serverless architecture and Lambda, containerization with ECS and EKS, and running containers without managing servers using Fargate.
topics.goal: Deploy a containerized workload on Fargate and a serverless function on Lambda, and explain when to choose each.

topics.title: Messaging & Application Integration
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: SQS, SNS, EventBridge: decoupling apps with queues and event routing
topics.description: Decoupling applications with SQS queues, SNS pub/sub notifications, and EventBridge event routing — and when to use each.
topics.goal: Design a decoupled architecture using SQS and SNS for a workload with unpredictable traffic spikes.

topics.title: Security, Identity & Compliance
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: IAM & shared model
topics.description: The AWS shared responsibility model, IAM users/groups/roles/policies, protecting data in transit and at rest, and detecting and responding to security events.
topics.goal: Apply least-privilege IAM policies and explain which security responsibilities are AWS's versus the customer's.

topics.title: Monitoring & Governance
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: CloudWatch & CloudTrail: metrics, alarms, auditing, and governance
topics.description: Observability with CloudWatch metrics, logs, and alarms; auditing with CloudTrail; multi-account governance with Organizations; and proactive guidance from Trusted Advisor.
topics.goal: Set up a CloudWatch alarm and explain how CloudTrail supports a compliance audit.

topics.title: Pricing, Billing & Support
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Free Tier & cost
topics.description: The AWS Free Tier, core pricing concepts (pay-as-you-go, pay-less-by-using-more), Billing and Cost Explorer, AWS Support plans, and everyday cost optimization techniques.
topics.goal: Use AWS Cost Explorer and Budgets to identify and reduce an overspend, and pick the right Support plan for a scenario.

topics.title: Migration & Emerging Services
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: CAF, Snow Family, AI: migration strategy and emerging AWS services
topics.description: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework and the 6 R's of migration, the Snow Family for offline data transfer, and an overview of AWS's AI/ML and generative AI services.
topics.goal: Recommend a migration strategy (rehost, replatform, refactor, etc.) for a legacy on-premises application.

topics.title: Well-Architected Framework & Exam Prep
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: 6 pillars & exam prep for the AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner exam
topics.description: The six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework, applying them to real architectures, and a final review of AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner exam domains and question patterns.
topics.goal: Evaluate a sample architecture against the six Well-Architected pillars and identify its weakest pillar.

topics.title: The Client-Server Model
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: How a browser talks to a server: the request/response cycle
topics.description: What a 'server' actually is, and the request/response cycle every website relies on — your browser asks, a server answers.
topics.goal: Learner can explain, in plain terms, what happens between clicking a link and a page appearing.

topics.title: Anatomy of a URL
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Protocol, host, path, and every part of a URL explained
topics.description: Every part of a URL, from the protocol at the front to the fragment at the end, and what each piece actually tells the browser to do.
topics.goal: Learner can break down any URL into its protocol, host, port, path, query string, and fragment.

topics.title: HTTP vs HTTPS
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: What the 's' actually protects, and why the padlock matters
topics.description: What changes when a site uses HTTPS instead of HTTP, why the padlock icon matters, and what a certificate is protecting you from.
topics.goal: Learner can explain why HTTPS matters and identify when a connection is not secure.

topics.title: Domains & Subdomains
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: TLDs, registrars, and how subdomains split a domain
topics.description: What a domain name actually is, how top-level domains and registrars work, and how subdomains split up a single domain.
topics.goal: Learner can distinguish a domain, a subdomain, and a top-level domain from a real-world URL.

topics.title: Browsers & Private Browsing
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Cache, cookies, and what incognito mode does and doesn't do
topics.description: What a browser stores between visits — cache, cookies, history — and exactly what private or incognito mode does and doesn't protect you from.
topics.goal: Learner can correctly explain what incognito mode hides, and from whom.

topics.title: Hosting Models
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Shared, VPS, cloud, and static hosting trade-offs
topics.description: The main ways a website gets hosted — shared hosting, a VPS, cloud platforms, and static hosting — and the real trade-offs between them.
topics.goal: Learner can recommend a hosting model for a given site based on its traffic and complexity.

topics.title: DNS & Domain Registration
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: A, CNAME, MX records, and how DNS propagation works
topics.description: How DNS turns a domain name into a server's IP address, the most common record types, and why changes take time to propagate.
topics.goal: Learner can choose the correct DNS record type to point a domain at a server or mail provider.

topics.title: SSL/TLS & HTTPS Setup
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Certificates, CAs, and free options like Let's Encrypt
topics.description: How an SSL/TLS certificate actually secures a connection, what a certificate authority does, and how free options like Let's Encrypt changed the game.
topics.goal: Learner can explain what happens when a browser encounters an invalid or expired certificate.

topics.title: Linux Hosting Basics
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: SSH, permissions, and what Apache or Nginx actually does
topics.description: The basics of managing a website on a Linux server — connecting over SSH, understanding file permissions, and what software like Apache or Nginx is actually doing.
topics.goal: Learner can describe the role a web server process plays in serving a website's files to visitors.

topics.title: CORS Explained
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Same-origin policy and common CORS misconfigurations
topics.description: Why browsers block requests between different origins by default, what CORS headers change about that, and the most common misconfigurations.
topics.goal: Learner can diagnose a CORS error and identify the correct server-side fix.

topics.title: Database & CMS Setup
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Provisioning a DB and when a CMS beats custom code
topics.description: The basics of setting up a database for a live website, keeping it secure, and when a CMS like WordPress is a better choice than custom code.
topics.goal: Learner can list the minimum steps to safely provision a database for a new website.

topics.title: Closures & the Scope Chain
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Closures & scope
topics.description: Understand how JavaScript's lexical scoping works under the hood and how closures form when a function retains access to its outer scope. Learn to use closures deliberately for data privacy, factory functions, and memoization.
topics.goal: Explain why a closure retains its outer variables after the outer function returns, build a counter factory using a closure, and identify a memory leak caused by an unintended closure reference.

topics.title: Prototypes, OOP & Classes
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: OOP & prototypes
topics.description: Understand JavaScript's prototype-based inheritance model: the prototype chain, Object.create, constructor functions, and ES6 class syntax as syntactic sugar over prototypes. Build class hierarchies with extends and super.
topics.goal: Create a class hierarchy using extends and super, explain what Object.getPrototypeOf returns for an instance, and convert a constructor-function pattern to an ES6 class.

topics.title: The `this` Keyword in Depth
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: this & binding
topics.description: Master JavaScript's four this binding rules: default, implicit, explicit (call/apply/bind), and arrow function binding. Understand how this behaves in callbacks, event handlers, class methods, and nested functions.
topics.goal: Predict what this refers to in five different call contexts, fix a broken event handler where this is undefined, and correctly bind a class method for use as a callback.

topics.title: Regular Expressions
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Regex patterns
topics.description: Write and interpret regular expressions for pattern matching, string validation, search-and-replace, and data extraction. Cover character classes, quantifiers, groups, lookaheads, and the global, case-insensitive, and multiline flags.
topics.goal: Write a regex that validates an email address, extract all hashtags from a text string, and replace phone number formats using a capture group.

topics.title: The Event Loop & Async Internals
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Event loop internals: call stack, task queue, microtasks
topics.description: Understand how JavaScript's single-threaded event loop runs concurrent-looking code: the call stack, task queue (macrotasks), microtask queue, and how Promises, queueMicrotask, and setTimeout interact at runtime.
topics.goal: Predict the output order of a snippet mixing setTimeout, Promise.resolve(), and sync code; explain why a long sync computation blocks the UI; and describe what queueMicrotask does differently from setTimeout(fn, 0).

topics.title: Iterators, Generators & Lazy Sequences
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Generators & iterables for lazy sequences and async iteration
topics.description: Build custom iterables using the iterator protocol (Symbol.iterator, next()), write generator functions for lazy sequences and async iteration, and understand how for...of and spread work with custom iterables.
topics.goal: Write a generator that yields paginated API results lazily, make a custom class iterable with for...of, and convert a recursive tree traversal into a generator.

topics.title: Advanced Object Patterns
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Proxy, Reflect & descriptors: intercepting object operations
topics.description: Use Proxy and Reflect to intercept and customize object operations. Understand property descriptors (enumerable, writable, configurable), Object.defineProperty, and the difference between Object.freeze, seal, and preventExtensions.
topics.goal: Build a validation Proxy that throws on invalid property writes, create a computed read-only property with Object.defineProperty, and explain the difference between a frozen and a sealed object.

topics.title: Performance & Memory Management
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Performance patterns: debounce, throttle, memoize, memory leaks
topics.description: Write performant JavaScript: debounce and throttle event handlers, memoize expensive functions, use requestAnimationFrame for smooth animations, and avoid common memory leak patterns. Profile with browser DevTools.
topics.goal: Implement a debounced search input and a throttled scroll handler, memoize a recursive function, and identify a memory leak in a DevTools heap snapshot.

topics.title: Testing JavaScript
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Unit testing with Jest: matchers, mocking, and async tests
topics.description: Write unit tests with Jest: describe/it structure, matchers (toBe, toEqual, toThrow), mocking modules and functions with jest.fn() and jest.mock(), and testing async code with async/await. Understand test coverage and TDD basics.
topics.goal: Write a test suite for a utility module covering happy paths, edge cases, and error throws; mock a fetch call and assert on call arguments; and achieve >90% coverage on a small module.

topics.title: Advanced Browser APIs
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Browser APIs beyond fetch: observers, Web Workers, Broadcast Channel
topics.description: Go beyond fetch with modern browser APIs: Intersection Observer for lazy loading and infinite scroll, ResizeObserver for responsive components, Web Workers for off-main-thread computation, and the Broadcast Channel API for cross-tab communication.
topics.goal: Implement infinite scroll with Intersection Observer, move heavy processing off the main thread with a Web Worker, and communicate results back via postMessage.

topics.title: JavaScript Design Patterns
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Design patterns in JS: Module, Observer, Factory, Strategy
topics.description: Implement patterns most useful in real JavaScript codebases: Module (encapsulation via closures), Observer/EventEmitter (decoupling), Factory (object creation), Strategy (swappable algorithms), and Singleton.
topics.goal: Build a typed event emitter using Observer, refactor a conditional-heavy function with Strategy, and implement a module with private state using the Module pattern.

topics.title: Functional Programming in JavaScript
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Functional JS patterns: pure functions, composition, currying
topics.description: Apply functional programming to JavaScript: pure functions, immutability, function composition, currying, partial application, and point-free style. Understand where FP patterns improve readability and testability versus where they add complexity.
topics.goal: Compose three pure functions into a data transformation pipeline, curry a binary function and partially apply it, and refactor a class with side effects into pure functions with dependency injection.

topics.title: Introduction to Jira & Agile Tracking
topics.label: Foundation
topics.description: Why teams use an issue tracker at all, how Jira fits into Agile/Scrum/Kanban practice, and how projects contain and organize work.
topics.goal: Learner can explain what problem Jira solves and how a project is structured inside it.

topics.title: Issues & Issue Types
topics.label: Foundation
topics.description: Story, Task, Bug, and Epic — the issue hierarchy (epic > story > subtask) and the core fields every issue carries.
topics.goal: Learner can pick the correct issue type for a given piece of work and explain how it relates to its epic.

topics.title: Writing Effective Tickets
topics.label: Foundation
topics.description: Clear titles and descriptions, acceptance criteria, labels, priority vs. severity, and components.
topics.goal: Learner can write a ticket that another engineer could pick up without needing to ask clarifying questions.

topics.title: Kanban Boards & Workflow States
topics.label: Foundation
topics.description: Columns and workflow transitions, WIP limits, and swimlanes on a Kanban board.
topics.goal: Learner can read a Kanban board and explain what a WIP limit is protecting the team from.

topics.title: Scrum Boards & Sprints
topics.label: Foundation
topics.description: Sprint planning, the sprint goal, product backlog vs. sprint backlog, and sprint length.
topics.goal: Learner can explain what happens during sprint planning and what a sprint goal is for.

topics.title: Backlog Management & Prioritization
topics.label: Foundation
topics.description: Backlog grooming/refinement, ranking, priority schemes, and linking stories to epics.
topics.goal: Learner can groom a messy backlog into a ranked, ready-for-sprint state.

topics.title: Reports & Agile Metrics
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.description: Burndown charts, velocity, cumulative flow diagrams, and sprint reports.
topics.goal: Learner can read a burndown chart and say whether a sprint is on track.

topics.title: Filters, JQL & Dashboards
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.description: Basic JQL (Jira Query Language) syntax, saved filters, and dashboard gadgets.
topics.goal: Learner can write a simple JQL query to find a specific set of issues.

topics.title: Collaboration & Issue Linking
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.description: Comments and mentions, issue links (blocks / relates to / duplicates), subtasks, and watchers.
topics.goal: Learner can model a real dependency between two issues using the correct link type.

topics.title: Running a Full Sprint Cycle
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.description: The end-to-end rhythm of a sprint: backlog refinement, sprint planning, daily execution, sprint review, and retrospective.
topics.goal: Learner can walk through an entire sprint from planning to retrospective and explain the purpose of each ceremony.

topics.title: Branching & Merging
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Branch workflows
topics.description: Understand how branches work, why feature branches are useful, and how to merge changes safely using merge commits or rebasing.
topics.goal: Apply branching strategies to manage parallel work and avoid conflicts.

topics.title: Remote Collaboration
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Push, pull, fetch
topics.description: Work with remote repositories using push, pull, fetch, and remotes. Covers tracking branches, pull requests, and resolving collaboration issues.
topics.goal: Collaborate with teammates using remote Git workflows.

topics.title: Merge Conflicts & Resolution
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Resolve conflicts
topics.description: Learn how merge conflicts occur and how to resolve them efficiently, including using Git tools and reviewing conflict markers.
topics.goal: Handle merge conflicts cleanly during branch integration.

topics.title: Parts of Speech & Word Basics
topics.label: Foundation
topics.description: Nouns, verbs, adjectives, pronouns, and articles — the basic building blocks of every English sentence, and how to identify and use each one correctly.
topics.goal: Identify the part of speech of a common word and use it correctly in a sentence.

topics.title: Sentence Structure & Basic Grammar
topics.label: Foundation
topics.description: How a correct English sentence is built — subject-verb agreement, simple and compound sentences, and the grammar mistakes that show up most often.
topics.goal: Write a grammatically correct sentence and spot a subject-verb agreement error in someone else's.

topics.title: Verb Tenses in Everyday Use
topics.label: Foundation
topics.description: Present, past, and future tenses as they are actually used in everyday speech and writing, including the tenses that trip people up most, like present perfect.
topics.goal: Choose the correct verb tense for a given everyday situation.

topics.title: Everyday Vocabulary Building
topics.label: Foundation
topics.description: Common everyday words, synonyms and antonyms, and different forms of the same word — building a vocabulary broad enough to express an idea without getting stuck.
topics.goal: Recognise and correctly use common synonyms, antonyms, and word forms instead of repeating the same word.

topics.title: Prepositions, Articles & Common Errors
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.description: The small words that cause the biggest grammar mistakes — in/on/at, a/an/the — and how to use them correctly and consistently.
topics.goal: Correctly choose prepositions and articles in everyday sentences, including the cases that most commonly get them wrong.

topics.title: Punctuation & Sentence Clarity
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.description: Commas, apostrophes, and capitalisation, and how to avoid run-on sentences and other punctuation mistakes that make writing harder to read.
topics.goal: Punctuate a short paragraph correctly and rewrite a run-on sentence into clear, separate sentences.

topics.title: Workplace & Professional Vocabulary
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.description: The vocabulary and phrasing that sound professional at work — replacing slang and filler words with clear, workplace-appropriate language.
topics.goal: Choose professional vocabulary over slang or filler in a workplace message or conversation.

topics.title: Reading Comprehension & Inference
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.description: Understanding written instructions, emails, and documentation accurately, and drawing correct conclusions from what is written rather than guessing.
topics.goal: Read a short passage or set of instructions and correctly answer a question that requires inference, not just recall.

topics.title: Professional Email & Written Communication
topics.label: Advanced
topics.description: Writing clear, well-toned professional emails — structure, tone, and the phrases that make a message easy to act on.
topics.goal: Identify or write a clear, professionally-toned email that gets its point across without ambiguity.

topics.title: Verbal Communication & Active Listening
topics.label: Advanced
topics.description: Speaking clearly, listening actively, and asking the kind of clarifying questions that prevent misunderstandings before they happen.
topics.goal: Recognise active listening in practice and identify the best clarifying question for a given situation.

topics.title: Communicating in Meetings & Teams
topics.label: Advanced
topics.description: Giving a clear status update, disagreeing respectfully, and stating an opinion professionally in a meeting or team discussion.
topics.goal: Choose the most professional way to disagree, give an update, or raise a concern in a meeting scenario.

topics.title: Explaining Technical Ideas Simply
topics.label: Advanced
topics.description: Structuring an explanation for someone without your technical background — cutting jargon without leaving out what actually matters.
topics.goal: Rewrite a jargon-heavy technical explanation into one a non-technical listener can follow.

topics.title: Remote & Cross-Cultural Communication Etiquette
topics.label: Advanced
topics.description: Communicating clearly in writing-first, asynchronous teams, and adjusting tone and expectations when working across cultures and time zones.
topics.goal: Choose communication habits that work well in a remote, asynchronous, and culturally diverse team.

topics.title: Modules: CommonJS & ESM
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: require vs import, .mjs/.cjs, and mixing module systems

topics.title: Error Handling & Resilience
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Custom errors, retries, circuit breakers, and graceful shutdown

topics.title: Security Fundamentals
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Secrets, injection risks, and securing a Node.js app

topics.title: Reading the Big Three Financial Statements
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: The P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement, and how they connect
topics.description: What the profit & loss statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement each actually show, how they relate to one another, and why a company can be 'profitable' on paper and still run out of cash.
topics.goal: Look at a simple set of financial statements and correctly identify what each one is telling you.

topics.title: Core Financial Vocabulary
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Revenue, margin, assets, liabilities, equity, and EBITDA
topics.description: The everyday financial vocabulary that shows up in every business conversation — revenue vs. profit, gross vs. net, assets vs. liabilities, equity, and what EBITDA means and why people use it.
topics.goal: Use core financial terms correctly and tell them apart when they sound similar.

topics.title: Profitability & Cost Analysis
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Margins, fixed vs. variable costs, and break-even thinking
topics.description: How to read gross margin and operating margin, tell fixed costs apart from variable costs, and work out a break-even point — the everyday toolkit for judging whether something is actually profitable.
topics.goal: Given basic cost and revenue figures, judge whether a product or initiative is profitable and why.

topics.title: Budgeting, Forecasting & Variance
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Building a budget, forecasting, and explaining a variance
topics.description: How budgets are built and used to track performance, the difference between a forecast and a budget, and how to explain a budget variance in a way that actually holds up.
topics.goal: Read a budget-vs-actual report and explain what a given variance means and what likely caused it.

topics.title: Investment Appraisal Essentials
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: ROI, payback period, and NPV/IRR at a working level
topics.description: The conceptual tools used to judge whether an investment is worth making — return on investment, payback period, and why NPV and IRR account for the time value of money in a way simpler measures don't.
topics.goal: Compare two investment options using ROI, payback period, and NPV/IRR reasoning and explain which is the stronger choice.

topics.title: Business Case & Financial Risk Analysis
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Stress-testing assumptions and framing financial risk
topics.description: How to build or critique a business case on financial grounds — questioning its assumptions, running a basic sensitivity analysis, and framing financial risk honestly instead of hiding it in a rosy forecast.
topics.goal: Critique a business case by identifying its weakest financial assumption and how sensitive the outcome is to it.

topics.title: What Is Artificial Intelligence?
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: AI vs. automation, narrow vs. general AI, and a brief history of the field
topics.description: Defines artificial intelligence in plain terms and distinguishes it from simple automation and rule-based software. Covers narrow AI vs. general AI, key historical milestones (the Turing test, expert systems, AI winters), and why AI is having a breakout moment now due to compute, data, and model advances.
topics.goal: Explain what AI actually is, distinguish it from ordinary automation, and describe why AI capabilities have accelerated so quickly in recent years.

topics.title: AI, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: How AI, ML, and deep learning nest inside each other and where they differ
topics.description: Clarifies the nested relationship between AI (the broad goal), machine learning (a method for achieving it), and deep learning (a specific ML technique using neural networks). Covers common terminology confusion and how these terms get used interchangeably despite meaning different things.
topics.goal: Correctly place AI, machine learning, and deep learning in relation to one another and use each term accurately in conversation.

topics.title: How a Machine Learns
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Training data, features, labels, and the three main ways ML models learn
topics.description: Explains the core ML workflow: training data, features, and labels, and how a model improves through exposure to examples. Covers the conceptual difference between supervised learning (labeled examples), unsupervised learning (finding patterns), and reinforcement learning (learning from feedback/reward).
topics.goal: Describe how a machine learning model learns from data and identify whether a scenario is supervised, unsupervised, or reinforcement learning.

topics.title: Neural Networks Explained
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Neurons, layers, weights, and activation — the building blocks of deep learning
topics.description: Introduces the neural network at a conceptual level: neurons, layers, weights, and activation functions, without requiring math. Covers why stacking many layers ("deep" learning) lets networks recognize complex patterns, with intuitive examples like image and speech recognition.
topics.goal: Describe what a neural network is and why "deep" learning refers to networks with many layers, without doing the underlying math.

topics.title: Data: The Fuel of AI
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Data quality, bias, and privacy — why AI is only as good as its training data
topics.description: Covers why data quality and quantity determine AI performance, what "garbage in, garbage out" means in practice, how bias enters training data and shows up in model behavior, and basic data privacy considerations when AI systems process personal information.
topics.goal: Explain why training data quality matters, recognize how bias can enter an AI system through its data, and identify basic privacy concerns.

topics.title: Understanding Large Language Models
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: What LLMs are, how they're trained, and the transformer idea behind them
topics.description: Introduces large language models — the technology behind ChatGPT, Claude, and similar tools: what they are, how they're trained on massive text corpora, and a conceptual, non-mathematical introduction to the transformer architecture and attention mechanism that makes modern LLMs possible.
topics.goal: Explain what an LLM is, how it's trained, and describe at a high level what makes the transformer architecture different from earlier approaches.

topics.title: How LLMs Generate Responses
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Tokens, next-token prediction, context windows, and why LLMs hallucinate
topics.description: Explains how an LLM actually produces a response: tokenization, next-token prediction, and the role of the context window. Covers why LLMs sometimes generate confident-sounding but incorrect answers ("hallucination") and how that connects to the way they generate text.
topics.goal: Explain how an LLM generates a response one token at a time and describe why hallucination happens, so you can reason about when to trust an AI answer.

topics.title: Prompt Engineering Essentials
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Writing clear prompts, few-shot examples, and iterating to better AI output
topics.description: Covers practical techniques for getting better results from an LLM: writing clear and specific prompts, the difference between system and user prompts, using few-shot examples to guide output format, and iterative refinement when the first response isn't right.
topics.goal: Write clear, specific prompts and iteratively refine them to reliably get useful output from an AI assistant.

topics.title: AI in Everyday Tools and Products
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Where AI already shows up in search, office tools, and developer workflows
topics.description: Surveys how AI is already embedded in common products: AI-assisted search, writing and office tool integrations, coding assistants, and customer support chatbots. Focuses on recognizing AI features you're likely already using and what's happening behind them.
topics.goal: Identify where AI is already embedded in tools you use daily and explain, at a high level, what's happening behind each feature.

topics.title: Generative AI Beyond Text
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Image, audio, video, and code generation, and multimodal AI systems
topics.description: Extends generative AI beyond chat: image generation models, AI-generated audio and video, code-generation assistants, and multimodal systems that combine text, image, and other inputs in a single model. Covers real-world use cases and current quality limits for each.
topics.goal: Describe how generative AI is used beyond text — for images, code, audio, and multimodal tasks — and where each is genuinely useful today.

topics.title: Where AI Excels vs. Where It Fails
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Real strengths, real limitations, and why human oversight still matters
topics.description: Provides a grounded assessment of AI capability: tasks where AI genuinely outperforms humans (pattern recognition at scale, drafting, summarization) versus tasks where it consistently struggles (nuanced judgment, factual reliability, true reasoning). Covers why human oversight remains essential.
topics.goal: Assess whether a task is well-suited to AI assistance and identify where human review and oversight are still required.

topics.title: AI Ethics and Responsible Use
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Bias, misinformation, copyright, privacy, and job impact considerations
topics.description: Covers the major ethical considerations around AI use: algorithmic bias and fairness, the risk of AI-generated misinformation, copyright and IP questions around training data and generated content, data privacy, and the impact of AI on jobs and skills.
topics.goal: Identify the major ethical risks associated with AI systems and apply basic responsible-use judgment when adopting AI tools at work.

topics.title: The AI Landscape and What's Next
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Major AI players, the rise of AI agents, and how to keep learning
topics.description: Surveys the current AI landscape at a conceptual level: the major model families and companies shaping the field, the emerging idea of AI agents that take multi-step actions rather than just respond to prompts, and practical suggestions for staying current as the field keeps moving.
topics.goal: Describe the current AI landscape and the shift toward AI agents, and identify practical ways to keep your AI knowledge current.

topics.title: WebSocket Protocol Fundamentals
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: The Upgrade handshake, frames, opcodes, and why persistent connections beat polling
topics.description: Why HTTP request/response doesn't fit real-time use cases, how a WebSocket connection is negotiated via the HTTP Upgrade handshake, the binary frame format (opcodes, fragmentation, masking), ping/pong keep-alives, and close codes. Also compares WebSockets against polling and Server-Sent Events.
topics.goal: Explain how a WebSocket connection is established and maintained at the protocol level, and choose the right transport for a given real-time requirement.

topics.title: Building Real-Time Servers with Socket.IO
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Namespaces, rooms, acknowledgements, middleware, and connection auth with Socket.IO
topics.description: Building a real-time Node.js server with Socket.IO: emitting and listening for events, organizing connections with namespaces and rooms, acknowledgement callbacks for request/response-style events over a socket, writing connection middleware, authenticating a socket handshake with a JWT, and Socket.IO's automatic fallback transports.
topics.goal: Build a Socket.IO server that organizes clients into rooms, authenticates connections, and reliably confirms delivery of events.

topics.title: Real-Time Architecture Patterns
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Pub/sub, broadcast vs. targeted emit, presence, and event-driven design for real-time systems
topics.description: Architectural patterns behind real-time features: publish/subscribe versus direct emit, broadcasting to a room versus targeting one socket, tracking who's online (presence), designing an event-driven flow instead of a request/response one, and when a message queue belongs between your services instead of a direct socket call.
topics.goal: Choose and apply the right real-time architecture pattern — pub/sub, broadcast, or presence tracking — for a given feature.

topics.title: Scaling & Securing WebSocket Connections
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Redis-backed multi-instance scaling, sticky sessions, reconnection, and real-time rate limiting
topics.description: Taking a WebSocket server to production: broadcasting across multiple server instances with a Redis adapter, sticky sessions and load-balancer configuration for stateful connections, handling reconnection and heartbeats gracefully, and defending against abuse with rate limiting and backpressure on socket events.
topics.goal: Run a WebSocket/Socket.IO server safely and correctly across more than one server instance, and harden it against disconnects and abuse.

topics.title: Execution Context & the Call Stack
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: How JS creates, stacks, and hoists execution contexts
topics.description: Understand how JavaScript creates an Execution Context for every script and function call, its two-phase lifecycle (creation, then execution), and how the Call Stack tracks nested calls and overflows. Learn how var and function hoisting differ from let/const, and why accessing a let or const before its declaration throws in the Temporal Dead Zone.
topics.goal: Trace the call stack through three nested function calls including a stack overflow case; explain why a hoisted var reads as undefined before its line while a hoisted let throws in the TDZ; and describe what a Lexical Environment holds during the creation phase.

topics.title: JavaScript Engines & JIT Compilation
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Inside V8: parsing, JIT compilation, and hidden classes
topics.description: Look inside engines like V8: how source code becomes bytecode through the parser and interpreter, how the Just-In-Time compiler promotes 'hot' functions into optimized machine code, and how hidden classes and inline caching make property access fast. Understand when the engine deoptimizes back to the interpreter and why.
topics.goal: Explain why calling a function with consistently-shaped objects is faster than mixing shapes; describe the round trip from source code to bytecode to optimized machine code; and identify a coding pattern that triggers a deoptimization.

topics.title: Memory Management & Garbage Collection
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: GC algorithms, WeakMap/WeakSet, and the JS heap
topics.description: Understand how the JavaScript heap allocates objects and how the garbage collector reclaims memory that is no longer reachable. Contrast the mark-and-sweep algorithm with reference counting, and see why reference counting alone cannot collect circular references. Learn how WeakMap and WeakSet let you associate data with an object without keeping it alive.
topics.goal: Explain why two objects that reference each other are still collected under mark-and-sweep but would leak under naive reference counting; rewrite a Map-based per-object cache as a WeakMap-based one so entries become collectible; and explain what a memory metric like performance.memory or a heap snapshot's retained size is actually measuring.

topics.title: Web Components
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Custom elements, Shadow DOM, and <template>/<slot>
topics.description: Build reusable, encapsulated custom elements using the Custom Elements API, Shadow DOM for style and DOM isolation, and <template>/<slot> for reusable markup structures -- the browser-native alternative to framework components.
topics.goal: Register a custom element with connectedCallback, attach a shadow root that isolates its internal styles from the host page, and use <template> with <slot> to let consumers project their own content into a reusable component.

topics.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: What ML is, how it learns, and the core vocabulary
topics.description: Learn what machine learning is and how a model learns from data. Covers: types of machine learning, features and labels, training vs inference, overfitting and underfitting, and the ML workflow.
topics.goal: You'll be able to explain how ML works in plain words and use its core terms correctly.

topics.title: Problem Framing and Baselines
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Turn a real problem into a clear ML task
topics.description: Learn how to turn a real-world problem into a clear ML task. Covers: choosing the task type, the target and inputs, success metrics, simple baselines, and when not to use ML.
topics.goal: You'll be able to frame a product problem as an ML task and judge whether ML is the right tool.

topics.title: Data Preparation
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Clean and transform raw data safely
topics.description: Learn how to clean and transform raw data so a model can learn from it. Covers: exploring a dataset, missing values, invalid records and outliers, encoding categories, and feature scaling.
topics.goal: You'll be able to clean and transform a raw dataset and explain why each step was needed.

topics.title: Statistics and Probability for ML
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Read data and results with the right statistics
topics.description: Learn the core statistics needed to read data and model results correctly. Covers: averages and spread, distributions, sampling, probability basics, and confidence and uncertainty.
topics.goal: You'll be able to tell whether a difference between two results is meaningful or just noise.

topics.title: Validation, Splits, and Data Leakage
topics.label: Foundation
topics.shortDesc: Test models honestly and avoid leakage
topics.description: Learn how to test a model honestly so its score reflects real use. Covers: train and test splits, cross-validation, time and group splits, data leakage, and the final test set.
topics.goal: You'll be able to choose the right way to split data and spot leakage before it skews results.

topics.title: Regression Models
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Predict numbers and analyse errors
topics.description: Learn how to predict numbers, such as prices, demand or delivery times. Covers: linear regression, Ridge and Lasso regularization, error metrics like RMSE and R², residual analysis, and model limitations.
topics.goal: You'll be able to build a regression model, compare it with a baseline, and explain its errors.

topics.title: Classification Models
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Predict categories and pick the right metric
topics.description: Learn how to predict categories, such as spam or not spam. Covers: logistic regression, kNN and SVM, the confusion matrix, precision and recall, and decision thresholds.
topics.goal: You'll be able to pick a classifier, choose the right metric, and set a sensible threshold.

topics.title: Decision Trees and Ensemble Methods
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Trees, random forests, and gradient boosting
topics.description: Learn the tree-based models behind most real-world tabular ML. Covers: how decision trees split, pruning, random forests, gradient boosting, and feature importance.
topics.goal: You'll be able to train and tune tree-based models and explain why ensembles beat a single tree.

topics.title: Feature Engineering and Pipelines
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Build better features and repeatable pipelines
topics.description: Learn how to create better features and make preprocessing repeatable. Covers: features from raw data, date and text features, feature selection, pipelines, and train and serve consistency.
topics.goal: You'll be able to build a reusable pipeline and show which features actually improve a model.

topics.title: Model Selection and Hyperparameter Tuning
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Compare and tune models fairly
topics.description: Learn how to compare models and tune their settings fairly. Covers: parameters vs hyperparameters, grid and random search, cross-validated tuning, learning curves, and overfitting the validation set.
topics.goal: You'll be able to run a fair model comparison, tune the best candidate, and report its score.

topics.title: Model Interpretation and Calibration
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Explain predictions and trust probabilities
topics.description: Learn how to explain a model's predictions and check its probabilities. Covers: feature importance, SHAP and LIME, probability calibration, errors across groups, and correlation vs causation.
topics.goal: You'll be able to explain why a model predicts what it does and whether its confidence holds.

topics.title: Clustering
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Group similar records without labels
topics.description: Learn how to group similar records when the data has no labels. Covers: k-means, hierarchical clustering, DBSCAN, choosing the number of clusters, and interpreting clusters carefully.
topics.goal: You'll be able to segment a dataset into meaningful groups and judge whether they are real.

topics.title: Dimensionality Reduction
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Simplify data while keeping what matters
topics.description: Learn how to shrink many features into a few that keep what matters. Covers: the curse of dimensionality, PCA, t-SNE and UMAP, feature selection vs extraction, and when reduction helps.
topics.goal: You'll be able to reduce a high-dimensional dataset and choose the right method for the job.

topics.title: Anomaly Detection
topics.label: Intermediate
topics.shortDesc: Spot rare events and balance false alarms
topics.description: Learn how to spot rare or unusual events, such as fraud or faults. Covers: types of anomalies, statistical methods, isolation forest, choosing thresholds, and false alarms vs missed events.
topics.goal: You'll be able to set up anomaly detection and balance alert volume against missed cases.

topics.title: Neural Network Foundations
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: How a neural network learns, step by step
topics.description: Learn how a neural network learns from data, step by step. Covers: neurons and layers, activation functions, loss functions, backpropagation and gradient descent, and regularization.
topics.goal: You'll be able to explain how a network predicts, measures its error, and adjusts its weights.

topics.title: Deep Learning Workflows
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Train, debug, and compare neural models
topics.description: Learn how to train and debug neural networks in practice. Covers: PyTorch and TensorFlow, batches and epochs, training and validation curves, early stopping, and when deep learning pays off.
topics.goal: You'll be able to run a small deep-learning experiment, read its curves, and judge the result.

topics.title: Computer Vision and CNNs
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Teach models to understand images
topics.description: Learn how neural networks understand and classify images. Covers: images as pixel arrays, convolution and pooling, CNN architectures, data augmentation, and transfer learning.
topics.goal: You'll be able to explain how a CNN sees an image and fine-tune a pre-trained model for a task.

topics.title: NLP, Embeddings, and Transformers
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Turn text into numbers models can use
topics.description: Learn how computers turn text into numbers they can work with. Covers: tokenization, word and sentence embeddings, semantic similarity, attention, and the transformer architecture.
topics.goal: You'll be able to use embeddings for semantic search and explain how transformers use context.

topics.title: LLM Applications and Evaluation
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Build and test LLM features
topics.description: Learn how to build applications with large language models and test them. Covers: prompting basics, retrieval-augmented generation, evaluating answers, hallucinations, and cost and latency.
topics.goal: You'll be able to design an LLM feature, test it on real examples, and guard against failures.

topics.title: Model Deployment and Serving
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Take a trained model into production
topics.description: Learn how to take a trained model into production safely. Covers: batch vs real-time inference, saving and versioning models, serving through an API, input contracts, and handling bad inputs.
topics.goal: You'll be able to choose a deployment approach and set up reliable predictions in production.

topics.title: Monitoring, Drift, and Maintenance
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Keep a deployed model healthy
topics.description: Learn how to keep a deployed model healthy over time. Covers: monitoring inputs and predictions, data and concept drift, performance decay, alerts and thresholds, and retraining triggers.
topics.goal: You'll be able to catch model problems early and decide when a model needs retraining.

topics.title: Responsible, Private, and Secure ML
topics.label: Advanced
topics.shortDesc: Build ML that is fair, private, and safe
topics.description: Learn how to build ML systems that are fair, private and safe to use. Covers: bias and fairness, privacy and data handling, adversarial attacks, human oversight, and model cards.
topics.goal: You'll be able to identify the main risks of an ML system and put sensible safeguards in place.
